# Setup

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load core packages for the analysis session
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)
library(rstatix)
library(glue)

# Source project-wide functions, themes, and colour palettes
source(here("scripts_notebooks", "required.R"))


```

# Functional enrichment

Unified pipeline for all 6 conditions (Fluad, Engerix B, S. aureus, E.
coli,Burn, Trauma). All conditions are loaded from the pre-merged DGE
file, then each analysis (BTM means, BTM GSEA, Hallmarks means,
Hallmarks GSEA) runs once on the combined data and produces a single
output file.

## Import all conditions

Load the pre-merged DGE file that already contains all 6 conditions with
consistent column names and pathogen labels.

```{r}
# Import annotation tables for BTMs and Hallmark gene sets
btm_annotation_genes <- read_csv(here("tables", "btm_annotation_genes.csv"))
msigdbr_grouped <- read_csv(here("tables", "msigdb_hallmarks_grouped_genes.csv"))

#Load DGE results
all_degs <- readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_limma_degs.rds"))

# Extract unique condition labels 
annotation_conditions <- all_degs %>%
  select(condition, timepoint, model = organism) %>%
  distinct()

#Filter timepoints combinations
conditions_filtered <- readRDS(file = here("tables", "all_human_mouse_correlation_filtered_inter_weighted_filtered.rds")) %>% 
  mutate(pathogen_human = case_when(pathogen_human == "Hepatitis B" ~ "HepB",
                              pathogen_human == "Staphylococcus aureus" ~ "S. aureus",
                              pathogen_human == "Escherichia coli" ~ "E. coli",
                              T ~pathogen_human),
          pathogen_human = fct_relevel(pathogen_human, "Influenza", "HepB", "S. aureus", "E. coli", "Burn", "Trauma")) %>% 
  select(treatment_human, treatment_mouse, pathogen_human, pathogen_mouse,
         pathogen_comparison, timepoint_comparison,
         timepoint_human, timepoint_mouse) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  #Define control
  select(pathogen = pathogen_human, timepoint_comparison) %>% 
  distinct()

# ── Load BTM (Blood Transcriptional Modules) results
# Load mean log2FC per BTM process, collapsed across genes within each module
dge_btm_mean_process <- readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_mean_process.rds")) 

# Load gene-level BTM membership
dge_btm_process_genes <- readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_process_genes.rds"))

dge_btm_process_genes_wide = readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_process_genes_wide.rds")) %>% 
  inner_join(conditions_filtered,
             by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison))

# Load pre-computed GSEA results
gsea_results <- readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_gsea_btm_results.rds"))

# Load BTM GSEA + matched results
dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide <- readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide.rds")) %>% 
  inner_join(conditions_filtered,
             by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison))

# Matched GSEA results where human and mouse timepoints have been aligned for direct comparison
gsea_btm_results_all_matched <- readRDS(here("tables", "all_human_mouse_gsea_btm_results_matched.rds")) %>% 
  inner_join(conditions_filtered,
             by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison))



```

# =========================

# Functional analysis

## Condition-wise analysis

### BTMs

BTMs correlation, intra- and inter-species Compare means and NES

#### Module-level, BTMs

Prepare the wide-format table of BTM mean log2FC and NES values for
human vs mouse comparison, then compute Pearson correlations between
organisms under three significance filters: all modules, modules
significant in mouse only, and modules significant in both. Assemble a
combined data frame with facet-ready labels for downstream plotting.



##### Mean Log2-FC

###### Correlation

####### Condition vs. Condition
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
# Correlation between modules ==================

# Conditions (No-control)
# Compute correlation between human and mouse mean log2FC across all modules (no filtering)
cor_labels =      
  dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = mean_log2fc_Human,
    y_col = mean_log2fc_Mouse,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  )

# Compute correlation restricted to modules significant in mouse (p_adjust <= 0.25)
cor_labels_Mouse <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  filter(p_adjust_mean_Mouse <= 0.25) %>%
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = mean_log2fc_Human,
    y_col = mean_log2fc_Mouse,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  ) 


# Compute correlation restricted to modules significant in both human and mouse
cor_labels_Mouse_Human <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  filter(p_adjust_mean_Mouse <= 0.25, p_adjust_mean_Human <= 0.25) %>%
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = mean_log2fc_Human,
    y_col = mean_log2fc_Mouse,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  )

#Bind to one df
cor_labels_mean_long = bind_rows(cor_labels %>% mutate(filter = "All"), 
                                cor_labels_Mouse %>% mutate(filter = "Mouse"), 
                                cor_labels_Mouse_Human %>% mutate(filter = "Mouse and Human")) %>% 
  #Refactor
  mutate(pathogen = fct_relevel(pathogen, "Influenza", "HepB", "S. aureus", "E. coli", "Burn", "Trauma"),
         treatment = case_when(pathogen %in% c("HepB", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
                               pathogen %in% c("S. aureus", "E. coli") ~ "Infection",
                               pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") ~ "Injury",
                               TRUE ~ pathogen),
         treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury"))

# Join GSEA table with all three correlation summaries
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  # Reorder module groups and wrap long process names for display
  mutate(group = fct_relevel(group, c(immune_order)),
         process = str_wrap(process, width = 15)) %>%
  drop_na(mean_log2fc_Mouse) %>%
  # Attach the three sets of correlation labels by (pathogen, timepoint_comparison
  inner_join(cor_labels, by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  inner_join(cor_labels_Mouse %>% 
                dplyr::rename_with(
                .fn = ~ stringr::str_c(.x, "_filter_Mouse"),
                .cols = cor_value:cor_label
              ), by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  inner_join(cor_labels_Mouse_Human %>% 
                dplyr::rename_with(
                .fn = ~ stringr::str_c(.x, "_filter_Mouse_Human"),
                .cols = cor_value:cor_label
              ), by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  
  
  # Combine the three correlation labels into a single facet annotation
  mutate(cor_labels_all_filtered = paste0("All: ", cor_label, ",\nM: ", cor_label_filter_Mouse, ",\nM&H: ", cor_label_filter_Mouse_Human),
         facet_name = paste0(timepoint_comparison, "\n", cor_labels_all_filtered),
         pathogen = fct_relevel(pathogen, "Influenza", "HepB", "S. aureus", "E. coli", "Burn", "Trauma"),
         treatment = case_when(pathogen %in% c("Hep B", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
                               pathogen %in% c("S. aureus", "E. coli") ~ "Infection",
                               pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") ~ "Injury",
                               TRUE ~ pathogen),
         treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury"))

# Check
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df %>%
  dplyr::count(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)

```

Conditions vs. Control

```{r}

# Conditions vs. Control =======
# Compute correlation between human and mouse mean log2FC across all modules (no filtering)
cor_labels_control =      
  dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = mean_log2fc_Human,
    y_col = mean_log2fc_Control,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  )

# Compute correlation restricted to modules significant in mouse (p_adjust <= 0.25)
cor_labels_Mouse_control <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  filter(p_adjust_mean_Mouse <= 0.25) %>%
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = mean_log2fc_Human,
    y_col = mean_log2fc_Control,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  ) 


# Compute correlation restricted to modules significant in both human and mouse
cor_labels_Mouse_Human_control <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  filter(p_adjust_mean_Mouse <= 0.25, p_adjust_mean_Human <= 0.25) %>%
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = mean_log2fc_Human,
    y_col = mean_log2fc_Control,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  )

#Bind to one df
cor_labels_mean_long_control = bind_rows(cor_labels_control %>% mutate(filter = "All"), 
                                cor_labels_Mouse_control %>% mutate(filter = "Mouse"), 
                                cor_labels_Mouse_Human_control %>% mutate(filter = "Mouse and Human")) %>% 
  #Refactor
  mutate(pathogen = fct_relevel(pathogen, "Influenza", "HepB", "S. aureus", "E. coli", "Burn", "Trauma"),
         treatment = case_when(pathogen %in% c("HepB", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
                               pathogen %in% c("S. aureus", "E. coli") ~ "Infection",
                               pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") ~ "Injury",
                               TRUE ~ pathogen),
         treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury"))



# Join GSEA table with all three correlation summaries
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df_control <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  # Reorder module groups and wrap long process names for display
  mutate(group = fct_relevel(group, c(immune_order)),
         process = str_wrap(process, width = 15)) %>%
  drop_na(mean_log2fc_Control) %>%
  # Attach the three sets of correlation labels by (pathogen, timepoint_comparison
  inner_join(cor_labels_control, by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  inner_join(cor_labels_Mouse_control %>% 
                dplyr::rename_with(
                .fn = ~ stringr::str_c(.x, "_filter_Mouse"),
                .cols = cor_value:cor_label
              ), by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  inner_join(cor_labels_Mouse_Human_control %>% 
                dplyr::rename_with(
                .fn = ~ stringr::str_c(.x, "_filter_Mouse_Human"),
                .cols = cor_value:cor_label
              ), by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  
  
  # Combine the three correlation labels into a single facet annotation
  mutate(cor_labels_all_filtered = paste0("All: ", cor_label, ",\nM: ", cor_label_filter_Mouse, ",\nM&H: ", cor_label_filter_Mouse_Human),
         facet_name = paste0(timepoint_comparison, "\n", cor_labels_all_filtered),
         pathogen = fct_relevel(pathogen, "Influenza", "HepB", "S. aureus", "E. coli", "Burn", "Trauma"),
         treatment = case_when(pathogen %in% c("Hep B", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
                               pathogen %in% c("S. aureus", "E. coli") ~ "Infection",
                               pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") ~ "Injury",
                               TRUE ~ pathogen),
         treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury"))

# Check
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df_control %>%
  dplyr::count(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)
```



###### Heatmap of summary results
```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=14}

#Merge to one DF
cor_labels_mean_long_condition_control = bind_rows(cor_labels_mean_long,
                                                  cor_labels_mean_long_control %>% 
                                                    mutate(timepoint_comparison = "Control"))


# Data preparation
correlation_long_all_btm_mouse_human_timepoints_summary_heatmap_mean = cor_labels_mean_long_condition_control %>%
  mutate(filter = str_replace(filter, "Mouse and Human", "Mouse\nand\nHuman"),
         timepoint_comparison = fct_relevel(timepoint_comparison, "Control")) %>% 
  # Aesthetics
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = timepoint_comparison,
      y = filter %>% fct_rev(),
      fill = cor_value) +
  # Facets
  facet_nested_wrap(~treatment+pathogen,
                    scales = "free_x",
                    nrow = 1) +
  # Geoms
  geom_point(aes(size = n_obs),
             pch = 21) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("r=",round(cor_value,2), ", R²=", round(r_squared,2))),
            color = "black",
            vjust = -2.5, fontface = "plain",
            size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n=", n_obs)),
            color = "black",
            vjust = 0.5, fontface = "plain",
            hjust = -0.5,
            size = 3)+
  # Scales
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 10)) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
    colors = c("#4DBBD5FF", "white", "#4361ee"),
    values = scales::rescale(c(-1, 0, 1)),
    limits = c(-1, 1),
    name = "Correlation",
    guide = ggplot2::guide_colorbar(
      barwidth = 10,
      barheight = 1,
      nbin = 10,
      raster = FALSE
    )
  ) +
  # Labels
  labs(
    x = "Time",
    y = "Filter",
    color = "Correlation",
    size = "N genes") +
  # Theme
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0, size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0.1, 0, 0.1, unit = "cm"),
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, -10, 0),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        ggh4x.facet.nestline = element_line(colour = "black", linetype = 1)) 

# Render plot
correlation_long_all_btm_mouse_human_timepoints_summary_heatmap_mean 
   
 

# Save
correlation_long_all_btm_mouse_human_timepoints_summary_heatmap_mean %>%
  ggsave(filename = here("Figures",  "all_human_mouse_mean_btm_correlation_all_timepoints_summary_heatmap_filtered.png"),
         width = 14,
         height = 4)
```

####### Scatter plot 
```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=14, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Data preparation
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df <-
  bind_rows(
    # All modules (no filtering)
    dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df %>%
      mutate(filter = "All"),
    # Modules significant in mouse only (padj <= 0.25 in mouse, > 0.25 in human)
    dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df %>%
      filter(p_adjust_mean_Mouse <= 0.25, p_adjust_mean_Human > 0.25) %>%
      mutate(filter = "Mouse"),
    # Modules significant in both organisms
    dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df %>%
      filter(p_adjust_mean_Mouse <= 0.25 & p_adjust_mean_Human <= 0.25) %>%
      mutate(filter = "Mouse and Human"),
  )

# Scatterplot
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_plot <- dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_df %>%
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = mean_log2fc_Mouse,
      y = mean_log2fc_Human) +
  facet_nested_wrap(vars(pathogen, facet_name),
                    scales = "free",
                    nrow = 1,
                    strip = strip_nested(size = "variable")) +

  # Guide lines
  geom_abline(alpha = 0.2, linetype = 2) +
  geom_abline(alpha = 0.2, linetype = 2, slope = -1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, alpha = 0.2, linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, alpha = 0.2, linetype = 2) +

  # Geom layer: all modules shown with blur for background density
  with_blur(
    geom_point(aes(fill = group, color = group, shape = filter),
               data = . %>% filter(filter == "All"),
               size = 2, alpha = 0.2, stroke = 0.1, sigma = 2)
  ) +

  # Geom layer: mouse-only significant modules drawn with full opacity
  geom_point(aes(fill = group, shape = filter, color = group),
             data = . %>% filter(filter == "Mouse"),
             size = 2, stroke = 0.1, alpha = 1) +

  # Geom layer: both-significant modules drawn with black outline for emphasis
  geom_point(aes(fill = group, shape = filter),
             color = "black",
             data = . %>% filter(filter == "Mouse and Human"),
             size = 2, stroke = 0.1, alpha = 1) +

  # Scales
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22, 24)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = immune_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = immune_colors) +
  guides(color = FALSE,
         fill = guide_legend(byrow = TRUE, nrow = 3,
                             keywidth = unit(0.3, "cm"),
                             keyheight = unit(0.3, "cm"),
                             override.aes = list(size = 3, shape = 21, color = "black"),
                             default.unit = "cm"),
         shape = guide_legend(byrow = TRUE, nrow = 3,
                              keywidth = unit(0.3, "cm"),
                              keyheight = unit(0.3, "cm"),
                              override.aes = list(size = 3),
                              default.unit = "cm")) +

  # Labels
  labs(fill = "Group",
       shape = "Significance",
       y = "Human (Mean Log2FC)",
       x = "Model (Mean Log2FC)") +

  # Theme customization
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5),
        strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.spacing.x = unit(0, "cm"),
        legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "cm"),
        ggh4x.facet.nestline = element_line(colour = "black", linetype = 1),
        legend.box.spacing = unit(0, "cm"),
        panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0, unit = "cm"))

# Render plot
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_plot

# Save
dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_plot %>%
  ggsave(filename = here("Figures", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_mean_group_correlation_plot_filtered.png"),
         width = 14, height = 4)
```

##### Plot NES

Compute Pearson correlations between Human and Mouse NES values across
BTMs, stratified by pathogen and timepoint, for all genes and for
significance-filtered subsets.

Condition vs. Condition
```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=7}
# Correlation for all modules
cor_labels_nes <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = nes_Mouse,
    y_col = nes_Human,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  ) 

# Correlation for Mouse-significant modules
cor_labels_nes_Mouse <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  filter(p_adjust_Mouse <= 0.25) %>% 
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = nes_Mouse,
    y_col = nes_Human,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  )

# Correlation for both Mouse and Human significant modules 
cor_labels_nes_Mouse_Human <- dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  filter(p_adjust_Mouse <= 0.25, p_adjust_Human <= 0.25) %>% 
  calculate_weighted_correlation_pearson(
    x_col = nes_Mouse,
    y_col = nes_Human,
    weight_col = weight_joint_gsea_fdr,
    group_cols = c("pathogen", "timepoint_comparison")
  ) 

#Bind to one df
cor_labels_nes_long = bind_rows(cor_labels_nes %>% mutate(filter = "All"), 
                                cor_labels_nes_Mouse %>% mutate(filter = "Mouse"), 
                                cor_labels_nes_Mouse_Human %>% mutate(filter = "Mouse and Human")) %>% 
  #Refactor
  mutate(pathogen = fct_relevel(pathogen, "Influenza", "HepB", "S. aureus", "E. coli", "Burn", "Trauma"),
         treatment = case_when(pathogen %in% c("HepB", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
                               pathogen %in% c("S. aureus", "E. coli") ~ "Infection",
                               pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") ~ "Injury",
                               TRUE ~ pathogen),
         treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury"))



# Build master correlation data frame with scores and annotations
dge_btm_nes_group_correlation_df = dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Reorder module groups and wrap long process names for display
  mutate(group = fct_relevel(group, c(immune_order)),
         process = str_wrap(process, width = 15)) %>%
  drop_na(mean_log2fc_Mouse) %>%
  
  # Attach the three sets of correlation labels by (pathogen, timepoint_comparison
  inner_join(cor_labels_nes, by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  inner_join(cor_labels_nes_Mouse %>% 
              dplyr::rename_with(
                .fn = ~ stringr::str_c(.x, "_filter_Mouse"),
                .cols = cor_value:cor_label
              ), by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  inner_join(cor_labels_nes_Mouse_Human %>% 
              dplyr::rename_with(
                .fn = ~ stringr::str_c(.x, "_filter_Mouse_Human"),
                .cols = cor_value:cor_label
              ), by = join_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)) %>%
  
  
  # Combine the three correlation labels into a single facet annotation
  mutate(cor_labels_all_filtered = paste0("All: ", cor_label, ",\nM: ", cor_label_filter_Mouse, ",\nM&H: ", cor_label_filter_Mouse_Human),
         facet_name = paste0(timepoint_comparison, "\n", cor_labels_all_filtered),
         pathogen = fct_relevel(pathogen, "Influenza", "HepB", "S. aureus", "E. coli", "Burn", "Trauma"),
         treatment = case_when(pathogen %in% c("HepB", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
                               pathogen %in% c("S. aureus", "E. coli") ~ "Infection",
                               pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma") ~ "Injury",
                               TRUE ~ pathogen),
         treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury"))
```

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=10}
# Precision analysis by Mouse NES quartiles

# Compute precision per quartile
results_quartiles = dge_btm_nes_group_correlation_df %>%
  # Retain only all-module filter; exclude pathogens with few timepoints
  # filter(!pathogen %in% c("Influenza", "Hepatitis B")) %>%
  # Stratify by pathogen and timepoint
  group_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison) %>%
  # Restrict to positively enriched modules only
  filter(nes_Mouse > 0,
         nes_Human > 0) %>%
  # Divide modules into quartiles by Mouse NES
  mutate(quartile = ntile(nes_Mouse, 4)) %>%
  # Compute precision per quartile
  group_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison, quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    total_in_quartile = n(),
    true_positives = sum(p_adjust_Human <= 0.05),
    precision_pct = (true_positives / total_in_quartile) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Visualisation: precision ladder plot
ggplot(results_quartiles) +
  aes(x = precision_pct, y = as.character(quartile), fill = as.character(quartile)) +
  # Geoms
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  # Reference line for random chance (5% = 0.05 alpha)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  # Facets
  facet_wrap(~pathogen, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  # Scales
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Mouse Quartile", option = "mako", direction = -1) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  # Theme
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
  # Labels
  labs(title = "Precision by Mouse NES Quartile",
       subtitle = "Higher Quartiles (4) should show higher % of Human validation",
       x = "Precision (% of BTMs Significant in Human)",
       y = "Timepoint")
```

#### Gene-level, BTMs

Reshape the per-gene matched expression data to wide format (one column
per organism) for subsequent correlation analysis.

```{r}
# Prepare data: wide format

# For each process, reshape matched expression to wide
dge_btm_process_genes_wide 
# Verify all pathogen-timepoint combinations present
dge_btm_process_genes_wide %>%
  dplyr::count(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)
```

Compute Spearman correlations between Human and Mouse gene expression
within each BTM, stratified by pathogen and timepoint.

```{r}
# Define a safe correlation function robust to low n and zero variance
safe_cor_test <- function(x, y, method) {
  # Remove non-finite values
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  x <- x[ok]
  y <- y[ok]
  # Require at least 3 observations and non-zero variance
  if (length(x) < 3 || sd(x) == 0 || sd(y) == 0) {
    return(list(estimate = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_))
  } else {
    tryCatch({
      ct <- cor.test(x, y, method = method)
      return(list(estimate = unname(ct$estimate), p.value = ct$p.value))
    }, error = function(e) {
      return(list(estimate = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_))
    })
  }
}

# Compute per-BTM Spearman correlation
dge_btm_process_genes_correlation <- dge_btm_process_genes_wide %>%
  # Group by BTM, pathogen, and timepoint
  group_by(pathogen, timepoint_comparison, process) %>%
  # Compute correlation and count genes
  summarise(
    n_genes = n(),
    test_result = list(safe_cor_test(x = mean_l2fc_Mouse, y = mean_l2fc_Human, method = "spearman")),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Extract correlation estimate and p-value
  mutate(
    cor_value = map_dbl(test_result, ~ .x$estimate %||% NA_real_),
    p_value   = map_dbl(test_result, ~ .x$p.value %||% NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  # Compute R-squared and significance label
  mutate(
    r_squared = cor_value^2,
    p_label = case_when(
      p_value <= 0.01 ~ "***",
      p_value <= 0.05 ~ "**",
      p_value <= 0.10 ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ "ns"
    ),
    cor_label = sprintf("r=%.2f, R²=%.2f, %s", cor_value, r_squared, p_label)
  ) %>%
  # Remove nested column and organise
  select(-test_result) %>%
  arrange(timepoint_comparison) %>%
  distinct()

# Inspect and save per-BTM correlation
dge_btm_process_genes_correlation %>%
  dplyr::count(pathogen, timepoint_comparison)

dge_btm_process_genes_correlation %>%
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_process_genes_correlation.rds"))

# Compute per-gene Spearman correlation across conditions
dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene <- dge_btm_process_genes_wide %>%
  # Select relevant columns; exclude Influenza and Hepatitis B
  select(symbol, pathogen, timepoint_comparison, Mouse = mean_l2fc_Mouse, Human = mean_l2fc_Human) %>%
  filter(!pathogen %in% c("Influenza", "Hepatitis B")) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  # Group by gene symbol
  group_by(symbol) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pathogens = n(),
      test_result = list(safe_cor_test(x = Human, y = Mouse, method = "spearman")),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Extract correlation estimate and p-value
  mutate(
    cor_value = map_dbl(test_result, ~ .x$estimate %||% NA_real_),
    p_value   = map_dbl(test_result, ~ .x$p.value   %||% NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  # Compute R-squared and significance label
  mutate(
    r_squared = cor_value^2,
    p_label = case_when(
      p_value <= 0.01 ~ "***",
      p_value <= 0.05 ~ "**",
      p_value <= 0.10 ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ "ns"
    ),
    cor_label = sprintf("r=%.2f, R²=%.2f, %s", cor_value, r_squared, p_label)
  ) %>%
  # Remove nested column and sort by correlation strength
  select(-test_result) %>%
  arrange(cor_value) %>%
  distinct()

# Inspect and save per-gene correlation
dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene

dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene %>%
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene.rds"))
```

Compare the leading-edge genes (LEGs) from Human and Mouse GSEA to
classify each gene as shared, Human-only, or Mouse-only.

```{r}
# Split core enrichment genes into separate rows
gsea_btm_results_core = gsea_btm_results_all_matched %>%
  filter(p_adjust <= 0.25) %>%
  separate_rows(core_enrichment, sep = "/")

# Join Human and Mouse core enrichment genes
gsea_btm_results_core_joined =
  # Extract Human core genes
  gsea_btm_results_core %>%
  filter(organism == "Human") %>%
  select(pathogen, process, timepoint,
         gene = core_enrichment,
         set_size_human = set_size,
         p_adjust_human_gsea = p_adjust) %>%
  mutate(human_core = TRUE) %>%
  # Full join with Mouse core genes
  full_join(
    gsea_btm_results_core %>%
      filter(organism == "Mouse") %>%
      select(pathogen, process, timepoint,
             gene = core_enrichment,
             set_size_mouse = set_size,
             p_adjust_mouse_gsea = p_adjust) %>%
      mutate(mouse_core = TRUE),
    by = c("pathogen", "process", "timepoint", "gene")
  ) %>%
  # Classify each gene's conservation status
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      human_core == TRUE & mouse_core == TRUE ~ "Shared",
      human_core == TRUE & is.na(mouse_core) ~ "Human only",
      mouse_core == TRUE & is.na(human_core) ~ "Mouse only",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Arrange and attach functional group
  arrange(pathogen, timepoint, process, status) %>%
  inner_join(btm_annotation_genes %>% select(process, group),
             by = "process") %>%
  distinct()

# Inspect and save
gsea_btm_results_core_joined %>%
  dplyr::count(pathogen, timepoint)

gsea_btm_results_core_joined %>%
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "all_human_mouse_gsea_btm_results_core_joined.rds"))
```

Compare the log2FC and ranks of core (Leading Edge) genes between
species for a specific biological process. This analysis evaluates
whether transcriptional signatures are conserved at the individual gene
level within each enriched pathway.

```{r}
# Compare log2FC and ranks of Leading Edge genes across species
# Evaluate if Leading Edge (core) genes maintain consistent log2FC and ranks between species for a specific process
# 1. Define target process
process_selected <- "immune activation - generic cluster"
# Calculate shared Leading Edge genes from genes present in both arrays
df_legs_perc_legs_only = df_legs %>%
  # Arrange rows alphabetically by process
  arrange(process) %>%
  # Keep only genes classified as core enrichment
  filter(status != "Not core") %>%
  # Select relevant identifier columns
  select(symbol, pathogen, process, timepoint, status) %>%
  # Group by condition and core status
  group_by(pathogen, timepoint, process, status) %>%
  # Count number of genes per status group
  summarise(n_status = n()) %>%
  # Remove grouping
  ungroup() %>%
  # Group by condition only (collapsing status)
  group_by(pathogen, timepoint, process) %>%
  # Compute total core genes and percentage per status
  mutate(n_total = sum(n_status),
         n_status_perc = round((n_status / n_total), 2) * 100)

# Unite all data sources into a master data frame by sequential joins
df_legs <- dge_btm_process_genes_wide %>%
  # Commented out: filter(process == process_selected)
  
  # 2. Join with GSEA core enrichment (Leading Edge) genes
  full_join(
    gsea_btm_results_core_joined,
    # Commented out: filter(process == process_selected)
    by = join_by(pathogen, process, timepoint, symbol == gene)
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Integrate shared percentage metrics
  inner_join(
    df_legs_perc_legs_only %>%
      filter(status == "Shared") %>%
      rename(status_percent = status),
    by = join_by(pathogen, process, timepoint)
  ) %>%
  
  # 4. Integrate Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES)
  inner_join(
    dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      # Commented out: filter(process == process_selected)
      select(process, pathogen, timepoint, starts_with("nes_")),
    by = join_by(pathogen, process, timepoint)
  ) %>%
  
  # 5. Integrate correlation statistics
  inner_join(
    dge_btm_process_genes_correlation %>%
      select(timepoint, pathogen, process, cor_value, r_squared, p_label, cor_label),
    by = join_by(pathogen, process, timepoint)
  ) %>%

  # 6. Data cleaning and dynamic label generation for faceting
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("nes_"), ~ round(.x, 2)),
    status = if_else(is.na(status), "Not core", status),
    facet_label = sprintf(
      "%s\nShared = %s%%\nNES Mouse = %.2f\nNES Human = %.2f",
      timepoint, n_status_perc, nes_Mouse, nes_Human
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(timepoint) %>%
  mutate(facet_label = fct_inorder(facet_label)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  # Rank genes by log2FC within each condition group
  group_by(pathogen, process, timepoint) %>%
  # Drop genes not measured in both organisms
  drop_na(Mouse, Human) %>%
  mutate(Mouse_rank = rank(Mouse),
         Mouse_rank_p = rank(Mouse * -log(p_adjust_mouse_gsea)),
         Human_rank_p = rank(Human * -log(p_adjust_human_gsea)),
         Human_rank = rank(Human)
         ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Check distinct pathogen-timepoint combinations
dge_btm_gsea_mean_wide %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(pathogen, timepoint) %>%
  distinct()


# Prepare data for ranking and categorical grouping
# Reshape rank variables into long format
df_legs_ranked = df_legs %>%
  filter(process == process_selected) %>%
  select(symbol:timepoint, group.x,
         status, status_percent:facet_label,
         Mouse_rank:Human_rank) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "value",
    cols = c("Mouse_rank", "Human_rank",
             "Mouse_rank_p", "Human_rank_p"
             )
  ) %>%
  mutate(organism = if_else(str_detect(variable, "Mouse"), "M", "H")) %>%
  
  # Refine labels and categorical grouping (Vaccination, Infection, Injury)
  mutate(
    facet_label = sprintf(
      "%s\n%s\nShared = %s%%\nNES M=%.2f, H=%.2f",
      timepoint, cor_label, n_status_perc, nes_Mouse, nes_Human
    ),
    treatment = case_when(
      pathogen %in% c("Hepatitis B", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
      pathogen %in% c("Saureus", "Ecoli")         ~ "Infection",
      pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma")           ~ "Injury",
      TRUE                                        ~ pathogen
    ),
    treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury")
  ) %>%
  arrange(timepoint) %>%
  mutate(facet_label = fct_inorder(facet_label))
```

Barplot showing the percentage of shared Leading Edge genes per
condition. This visualization highlights how much of the core enrichment
signature is conserved between species across different timepoints and
pathogen treatments.

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=12}
# Plot percent of shared Leading Edge genes per condition
# 1. Prepare data for ranking and categorical grouping
legs_perc_barplot = df_legs_perc_legs_only %>%
  # 2. Assign treatment categories: Vaccination, Infection, Injury
  mutate(
    treatment = case_when(
      pathogen %in% c("Hepatitis B", "Influenza") ~ "Vaccination",
      pathogen %in% c("Saureus", "Ecoli")         ~ "Infection",
      pathogen %in% c("Burn", "Trauma")           ~ "Injury",
      TRUE                                        ~ pathogen
    ),
    treatment = fct_relevel(treatment, "Vaccination", "Infection", "Injury")
  ) %>%
  # Arrange timepoints in order
  arrange(timepoint) %>%
  # Filter to target process and exclude Vaccination and Trauma
  filter(process %in% c(process_selected),
         !treatment == "Vaccination",
         !pathogen == "Trauma"
         ) %>%
  # Data aesthetics
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = n_status_perc,
      y = fct_rev(timepoint),
      fill = status) +
  # Facets
  facet_nested_wrap(~treatment + pathogen,
             scales = "free",
             nrow = 1,
             strip = strip_nested(size = "variable")) +
  # Geoms
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  # Scales and Labels
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors$comparison) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(fill = "Core Status",
       y = "Timepoint",
       x = "Percent") +
  # Theme and Legend styling
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.2, "lines"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, -10, 0),
    ggh4x.facet.nestline = element_line(colour = "black")
  ) +
  # Add percentage labels on bars
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_status_perc, "%\n(", n_status, ")")),
            lineheight = 0.8,
            position = "fill",
            color = "white",
            fontface = "bold",
            hjust = 1,
            size = 3)
```

##### Annotate with sequence identity

Import human-to-mouse sequence identity data from Ensembl BioMart and
annotate BTM core enrichment genes with homology information. This
annotation enables correlation of sequence conservation with
cross-species transcriptional concordance.

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=12}
# Download sequence identity data from Ensembl BioMart
# http://www.ensembl.org/biomart/martview/cdbaeb7d08ea2dbc5bae9a1b0d6ad871?VIRTUALSCHEMANAME=default&ATTRIBUTES=hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.ensembl_gene_id|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.ensembl_gene_id_version|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.ensembl_transcript_id|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.ensembl_transcript_id_version|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.mmusculus_homolog_perc_id_r1|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.mmusculus_homolog_perc_id|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.mmusculus_homolog_associated_gene_name|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.mmusculus_homolog_orthology_type|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.mmusculus_homolog_canonical_transcript_protein|hsapiens_gene_ensembl.default.homologs.mmusculus_homolog_ensembl_gene&FILTERS=&VISIBLEPANEL=attributepanel
# Import and annotate

# Import BTM core enrichment results
gsea_btm_results_core_joined =
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "all_human_mouse_gsea_btm_results_core_joined.rds")) %>%
  distinct()

# Import BTM gene-level correlation data
dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene =
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "all_human_mouse_dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene.rds"))

# Import homolog alignment data
all_alignments = read_csv(here("tables", "human_to_mouse_alignment_mart_export.txt"))

# Import BTM gene annotations
btm_annotation_genes = read_csv(file = here("tables", "btm_annotation_genes.csv"))

# Annotate genes with sequence identity and BTM membership
# Build alignment-annotated dataset for core enrichment genes
alignments_human2mouse = all_alignments %>%
  # Clean column names
  clean_names() %>%
  # Keep only high-confidence orthologs
  filter(mouse_orthology_confidence_0_low_1_high == 1) %>%
  # Remove rows without mouse gene names
  drop_na(mouse_gene_name) %>%
  # Select identity, homology type, and gene name columns
  select(gene = mouse_gene_name, mouse_homology_type,
         identity_human2mouse = percent_id_query_gene_identical_to_target_mouse_gene,
         identity_mouse2human = percent_id_target_mouse_gene_identical_to_query_gene) %>%
  # Standardize gene names to uppercase
  mutate(gene = str_to_upper(gene)) %>%
  # Resolve multiple identity scores by taking the median per gene
  group_by(gene) %>%
  summarise(identity_human2mouse = median(identity_human2mouse)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Filter to only BTM core enrichment genes and append process membership
  inner_join(gsea_btm_results_core_joined,
             by = join_by(gene))

# Reference: all high-confidence orthologs in the database (unfiltered)
alignments_human2mouse_all = all_alignments %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  filter(mouse_orthology_confidence_0_low_1_high == 1) %>%
  drop_na(mouse_gene_name) %>%
  select(gene = mouse_gene_name, mouse_homology_type,
         identity_human2mouse = percent_id_query_gene_identical_to_target_mouse_gene,
         identity_mouse2human = percent_id_target_mouse_gene_identical_to_query_gene) %>%
  mutate(gene = str_to_upper(gene)) %>%
  # Resolve multiple identity scores by taking the median per gene
  group_by(gene) %>%
  summarise(identity_human2mouse = median(identity_human2mouse)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Commented out: biomaRt gene info retrieval (pre-computed and imported below)
# human_mart <- useMart("ensembl", dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl")
# gene_info_human = getBM(
#   attributes = c("hgnc_symbol", "gene_biotype", "go_id", "namespace_1003", "name_1006"),
#   mart = human_mart,
#   values = alignments_human2mouse_all$gene %>% unique(),
#   filters = "hgnc_symbol"
# ) %>%
#   rename(go_name = name_1006, go_domain = namespace_1003, gene = hgnc_symbol)
# gene_info_human %>% saveRDS(file = here("tables", "gene_info_human.rds"))

# Import pre-computed human gene information and join with alignment data
gene_info_human =
  readRDS(file = here("tables", "gene_info_human.rds")) %>%
  inner_join(alignments_human2mouse_all, by = "gene")
```


Integrate sequence identity with cross-species gene correlation,
organized by functional hierarchy. This prepares data for comparing
sequence conservation with gene-level expression concordance.

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=12}
# Establish process order based on median sequence identity
process_order_median = alignments_human2mouse %>%
  select(process, group, gene, identity_human2mouse) %>%
  group_by(process) %>%
  summarise(median = median(identity_human2mouse)) %>%
  arrange(median)

# Prepare the detailed process-level dataframe with correlation stats
alignments_human2mouse_process_cor = alignments_human2mouse %>%
  select(process, group, gene, identity_human2mouse) %>%
  mutate(process = fct_relevel(process, process_order_median$process),
         group = fct_relevel(group, group_order_mean$group) %>% fct_rev()) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  # Join with gene-level Spearman correlation results
  left_join(dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene,
             by = join_by(gene == symbol)) %>%
  drop_na(cor_value)

# Create a group-level summary dataset (duplicating group as process)
alignments_human2mouse_group_btm_summary_process = alignments_human2mouse %>%
  select(process, group, gene, identity_human2mouse) %>%
  mutate(group = fct_relevel(group, group_order_mean$group) %>% fct_rev()) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  left_join(dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene,
             by = join_by(gene == symbol)) %>%
  mutate(process = group,
         process = fct_relevel(process, alignments_human2mouse$group %>% unique())) %>%
  drop_na(cor_value)

# Bind both levels into a single dataframe for integrated plotting
alignments_human2mouse_process_cor_withsummary = alignments_human2mouse_process_cor %>%
  bind_rows(alignments_human2mouse_group_btm_summary_process)
```

Compare sequence identity distributions across high-level functional
groups (BTM groups). A violin-boxplot-pointrange composite visualizes
the density, quartiles, and bootstrapped mean of human-to-mouse sequence
identity per group.

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=4}
# Calculate the mean identity per group to define the plot order
group_order_mean = alignments_human2mouse %>%
  select(process, group, gene, identity_human2mouse) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(identity_human2mouse)) %>%
  arrange(mean)

# Create the distribution plot (Violin + Boxplot + Pointrange)
alignments_human2mouse_pointrange_group_btm = alignments_human2mouse %>%
  select(process, group, gene, identity_human2mouse) %>%
  # Reorder groups based on the previously calculated means
  mutate(group = fct_relevel(group, group_order_mean$group)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  # Data aesthetics
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = identity_human2mouse,
      y = group,
      fill = group,
      color = group) +
  # Geoms
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.1,
               width = 0.1,
               fill = NA,
               color = "white") +
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_boot",
               geom = "pointrange",
               size = 1,
               fatten = 0.5,
               color = "black", show.legend = F) +
  # Scales
  scale_fill_manual(values = immune_colors) +
  scale_color_manual(values = immune_colors) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
  # Theme
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0.3, 0, 0, unit = "cm"),
        legend.position = "none",
        legend.direction = "horizontal",
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        legend.box.margin = margin(0, 0, -10, 0),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        ggh4x.facet.nestline = element_line(colour = "black", linetype = 1)
  ) +
  # Labels
  labs(x = "% Identity (Human-to-Mouse)",
       y = NULL,
       color = "Group",
       fill = "Group")
```

Construct the global comparison dataframe integrating sequence identity,
BTM membership, and functional correlation across all genes. This
dataset classifies genes into Human-only, Mouse-only, Shared, Immune
BTM, Non-Immune BTM, and All categories for downstream conservation
analysis.

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
# Build the unified dataframe of all gene conservation values across categories
# 1. Construct the Global comparison dataframe (All genes vs BTMs vs Orthologs)
alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df = alignments_human2mouse %>% 
  select(gene:pathogen, timepoint, status) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(gene_set = "Human vs. Mouse") %>% 
  # Bind with specialized BTM categories
  bind_rows(
    alignments_human2mouse %>% 
      mutate(gene_set = "BTMs",
             # Aggregate BTM groups into functional "Immune" and "Non-Immune" blocks
             status = case_when(
               group %in% c("ENERGY METABOLISM", "ECM AND MIGRATION", "CELL CYCLE", 
                            "SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION", "PLATELETS") ~ "Non-Immune BTMs",
               group %in% c("NEUTROPHILS", "T CELLS", "MONOCYTES", "B CELLS", 
                            "INNATE RESPONSE", "NK CELLS", "IFN") ~ "Immune BTMs",
               TRUE ~ status)
      ) %>% 
      select(gene, status, identity_human2mouse, gene_set) %>% 
      distinct(),
    # Bind with the total ortholog reference set
    gene_info_human %>% 
      distinct() %>% 
      mutate(status = "All", gene_set = "All") %>% 
      select(gene, status, identity_human2mouse, gene_set) %>% 
      distinct()
  ) %>% 
  # 2. Relevel status for logical visualization flow
  mutate(status = fct_relevel(status, "Human only", "Mouse only", "Shared", 
                              "Immune BTMs", "ENERGY METABOLISM", "ECM AND MIGRATION", 
                              "CELL CYCLE", "SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION", "PLATELETS", "All")) %>% 
  # 3. Integrate with functional correlation results
  left_join(dge_btm_process_genes_correlation_bygene,
            by = join_by(gene == symbol)) %>% 
  filter(gene_set == "Human vs. Mouse" | !is.na(cor_value))

# 4. Calculate gene frequency (How many conditions/pathogens each gene appears in)
alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_nshared = alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df %>%
  # Filter to only status categories relevant for sharing analysis
  filter(status %in% c("Mouse only", "Human only", "Shared")) %>% 
  arrange(gene) %>% 
  select(gene, status) %>%
  # Count how many conditions each gene appears in per status category
  group_by(status, gene) %>% 
  summarise(n_conditions_status = n()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(gene) %>% 
  # Compute total conditions per gene and derive sharing proportion and ratio
  group_by(gene) %>% 
  mutate(ntotal = sum(n_conditions_status),
         nstatus_to_total_pct = (n_conditions_status/ntotal) %>% round(2),
         nstatus_to_total = paste0(n_conditions_status, "-", ntotal)) %>% 
  # Classify each gene as Shared or Not-shared across conditions
  mutate(is_shared = if_else(status == "Shared", "Shared", "Not-shared")) %>%
  group_by(gene, is_shared) %>%
  mutate(n_group = sum(n_conditions_status)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  mutate(
    n_shared = sum(n_conditions_status[status == "Shared"]),
    n_notshared = ntotal - n_shared,
    ratio_shared_notshared_pct = round(n_shared / n_notshared, 2),
    ratio_shared_notshared_pct = if_else(is.infinite(ratio_shared_notshared_pct), NA_real_, ratio_shared_notshared_pct),
    # Classify based on whether shared proportion exceeds not-shared proportion
    class = if_else(ratio_shared_notshared_pct >= 1, "Shared", "Not-shared")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  # Join back the identity and correlation values from the full dataset
  inner_join(alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df %>% 
               select(gene, identity_human2mouse, cor_value:cor_label) %>% 
               distinct(),
             by = "gene") %>% 
  # Append the All, Immune BTM, and Non-Immune BTM categories without sharing classification
  bind_rows(alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df %>%
              filter(status %in% c("All", "Immune BTMs", "Non-Immune BTMs")) %>% 
               select(status,gene, identity_human2mouse, cor_value:cor_label) %>% 
               distinct() %>% 
              mutate(is_shared = status,
                     class = status))

# Save the combined sharing and conservation table to disk
alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_nshared %>% 
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_nshared.rds"))

# 5. Final cleaned reference for identity distribution
alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_filtered = alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df %>% 
  select(gene, status, identity_human2mouse) %>% 
  distinct()

# Create a filtered dataset of exemplar genes based on identity and correlation
top_shared_notshared_genes = bind_rows(
    # Select top 50 shared genes with highest sharing ratio
    alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_nshared %>%
    select(gene, 
           class, n_conditions_status, n_shared, ntotal, cor_value, p_value, r_squared, cor_label, identity_human2mouse,  ratio_shared_notshared_pct) %>%
    arrange(-ratio_shared_notshared_pct, -n_shared) %>% 
    filter(class == "Shared",
           n_shared > 3) %>%
      arrange(-ratio_shared_notshared_pct) %>% 
    slice_head(n = 50) %>% 
      select(-n_conditions_status) %>% 
    distinct() %>% 
      arrange(-identity_human2mouse, -cor_value),
    
    # Select top 50 not-shared genes with lowest sharing ratio
    alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_nshared %>%
    drop_na(cor_value) %>% 
    select(gene, 
           n_shared, class,  n_notshared, identity_human2mouse, cor_value, p_value, r_squared, cor_label, ntotal,ratio_shared_notshared_pct) %>%
    arrange(ratio_shared_notshared_pct, -n_notshared) %>% 
    filter(class == "Not-shared",
           n_notshared > 3) %>%
    arrange(ratio_shared_notshared_pct) %>% 
      slice_head(n = 50) %>% 
    distinct(),
    
    # Include all Immune BTM, Non-Immune BTM, and All category genes
    alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_nshared %>%
      filter(status %in% c("Immune BTMs", "Non-Immune BTMs", "All")) %>% 
    drop_na(cor_value) %>% 
    select(gene, ntotal, 
           n_shared, class, n_notshared, identity_human2mouse, cor_value, p_value, r_squared, cor_label, ntotal,ratio_shared_notshared_pct) %>%
    distinct()
    ) %>% 
  mutate(n_conditions_is_shared = ntotal)

# Save the top exemplar gene table to disk
top_shared_notshared_genes %>% 
  saveRDS(file = here("tables", "top_shared_notshared_genes.rds"))
```

##### Scatterplots of top shared LEGs

Scatterplots comparing mouse versus human log2 fold changes for the top
shared Leading Edge Genes (LEGs). Each panel shows a single gene across
conditions, with points colored by pathogen and a linear regression line
indicating cross-species concordance.

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=4}
# Scatterplots of top shared LEGs ----
# Log2FC cross-species comparison for top shared LEGs ----
top_shared_notshared_genes %>%
                 ungroup() %>%
                 filter(class == "Shared") %>% 
  # Join species-specific log2FC values from the wide-format GSEA table
  inner_join(dge_btm_process_genes_wide %>% 
               select(gene = symbol, pathogen, timepoint, Mouse:adj_p_val_Human) %>% 
               distinct(),
             by = "gene") %>%
  # Retain only genes with strong cross-species correlation
  filter(r_squared > 0.2) %>% 
    # Exclude vaccination conditions to focus on infection-only comparisons
    filter(!pathogen %in% c("Influenza", "Hepatitis B")) %>% 
  ggplot() +
    aes(x = Mouse,
      y = Human) +
    # One panel per gene with its correlation label
    facet_wrap(~gene+cor_label, 
             scales = "free",
             ncol = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = pathogen),
             size = 3,
             pch = 21,
             color = "black") +
  # Linear regression line with confidence band
  stat_smooth(method = "lm",
              color = "black",
              fill = "gray",
              alpha = 0.2) +
  # Reference lines at zero
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors$pathogen) +
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(legend.position = "top") +
    labs(title = "Shared LEGs, R2 > 0.2",
       subtitle = "Without vaccination",
       fill = "Pathogen")





```

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=20}
nshared_shared_plot = (alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_nshared %>%

  aes(x = n_notshared,
```

Create a filtered dataset of exemplar genes based on identity and
correlation

```{r fig.height=5, fig.width=6}
# Build filtered exemplar gene dataset stratified by correlation direction and sequence identity
alignments_human2mouse_genes_filtered = bind_rows(

  # SHARED vs NOT-SHARED CATEGORY
  # Positive correlation, high identity (>90%)
  top_shared_notshared_genes %>%
    filter(p_value <= 0.10,
           cor_value >= 0, 
            r_squared > 0.2,
           ntotal > 3,
           identity_human2mouse > 90) %>% 
    group_by(class) %>%
    arrange(-cor_value, 
            -ntotal) %>%
    slice_head(n = 100) %>% 
    mutate(filter = "Positive correlation,\nHigh %Identity"),
  
  # Positive correlation, low identity (<90%)
  top_shared_notshared_genes %>%
    filter(ntotal > 3, 
           cor_value > 0,
           p_value <= 0.10,
            r_squared > 0.2,
           identity_human2mouse < 90) %>% 
    arrange(-cor_value, identity_human2mouse) %>% 
    group_by(class) %>% 
    slice_head(n = 100)  %>% 
    mutate(filter = "Positive correlation,\nLow %Identity"),

  # Negative correlation, high identity (>90%)
  top_shared_notshared_genes %>%
    filter(ntotal > 3,
           p_value <= 0.10, 
            r_squared > 0.2,
           cor_value < 0, 
           identity_human2mouse > 90) %>% 
    group_by(class) %>%
    arrange(cor_value, -ntotal) %>%
    slice_head(n = 100) %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    mutate(filter = "Negative correlation,\nHigh %Identity"),

  # Negative correlation, low identity (<90%)
  top_shared_notshared_genes %>%
    filter(p_value <= 0.10, 
           cor_value < 0, 
           r_squared > 0.2,
           ntotal > 3,
           identity_human2mouse < 90) %>% 
    group_by(class) %>%
    arrange(cor_value, -ntotal) %>%
    slice_head(n = 100) %>% 
    ungroup() %>% 
    mutate(filter = "Negative correlation,\nLow %Identity"),
  
  # BTM CATEGORY (Immune, Non-Immune, All)
  # Positive correlation, high identity (>90%) for BTM sets
  top_shared_notshared_genes %>%
    filter(class %in% c("Immune BTMs", "Non-Immune BTMs", "All"),
           p_value < 0.10,
            r_squared > 0.2,
           identity_human2mouse > 90,
           cor_value > 0,
           ) %>%
    group_by(class) %>%
    arrange(-cor_value, -ntotal) %>% 
    slice_head(n = 100) %>% 
    mutate(filter = "Positive correlation,\nHigh %Identity"),
  
  # Negative correlation, low identity (<90%) for BTM sets
  top_shared_notshared_genes %>%
    filter(class %in% c("Immune BTMs", "Non-Immune BTMs", "All"),
           p_value < 0.10,
           cor_value < 0,
            r_squared > 0.2,
           identity_human2mouse <90,
           ) %>%
    group_by(class) %>%
    arrange(-cor_value, -ntotal) %>% 
    slice_head(n = 100) %>% 
    mutate(filter = "Negative correlation,\nLow %Identity"),

) %>% 
  # Clean labels and reorder factors for consistent plotting
  mutate(
    class = str_replace(class, " ", "\n"),
    class = fct_relevel(class, "Not-shared", "Shared", 
                         "All", "Non-Immune\nBTMs", "Immune\nBTMs"),
    filter = fct_relevel(filter, 
                         "Positive correlation,\nHigh %Identity",
                         "Negative correlation,\nHigh %Identity", 
                         "Positive correlation,\nLow %Identity",
                         "Negative correlation,\nLow %Identity")
    )
```

##### Gene biotype

Examine whether gene biotype categories (miRNA, protein-coding,
pseudogenes, lncRNA, snoRNA) differ in their sequence identity to mouse
orthologs. This tests whether conservation level relates to functional
gene class.

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=4}
# Test whether gene biotype is associated with %Identity
gene_info_human %>% 
  select(hgnc_symbol, gene_biotype, identity_human2mouse) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  group_by(gene_biotype) %>% 
  mutate(median_identity = median(identity_human2mouse)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(gene_biotype %in% c("miRNA", "protein_coding",
                             "processed_pseudogene",
                             "snoRNA",
                             "lncRNA",
                             "unprocessed_pseudogene")) %>% 
  arrange(median_identity) %>%
  mutate(gene_biotype = fct_inorder(gene_biotype)) %>% 
  # Violin with overlaid boxplot for each biotype
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = identity_human2mouse,
      y = gene_biotype,) +
  geom_violin(fill = "#4DBBD5FF",
              alpha = 0.2,
              color = NA, width = 2) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3,
               fill = NA) +
  theme_vaxgo() +
  labs(x = "%Identity",
       y = "",
       title = "Biotype and %Identity of mouse orthologs")
```

##### Cellular component ontology

Evaluate sequence identity of Leading Edge Genes (LEGs) and other
categories across major subcellular compartments.

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=12}
# How LEGs are associated with identity by gene cellular component ontology
# Point-range plot of %Identity across gene categories, faceted by subcellular compartment

gene_info_human %>%
  # 1. Integrate GO annotations with global identity and status data
  inner_join(
    alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_filtered %>% 
      select(-identity_human2mouse),
    by = join_by("hgnc_symbol" == gene)
  ) %>% 
  
  # 2. Filter for specific Cellular Component domains
  filter(
    go_domain == "cellular_component",
    go_name %in% c("nucleus", "cytoplasm", "membrane", "extracellular region")
  ) %>% 
  
  # 3. Clean and reformat status labels for plotting
  select(hgnc_symbol, go_name, identity_human2mouse, status) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(status = str_replace(status, " ", "\n")) %>%
  mutate(status = fct_relevel(
    status,
    "Human\nonly", "Mouse\nonly", "Shared", "All", 
    "Non-Immune\nBTMs", "Immune\nBTMs"
  )) %>% 
  
  # 4. Visualization: Compare identity across GO categories using facets
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = status,
      y = identity_human2mouse,
      fill = status,
      color = status) +
  facet_wrap(~str_to_title(go_name),
             nrow = 1,
             axes = "all") +
  
  # 5. Statistical Summary: Mean and 95% CI via bootstrapping
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_boot",
               geom = "pointrange") +
  
  # 6. Styling, Scales, and Legends
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.text.x = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = colors$comparison) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colors$comparison) +
  labs(color = "Status",
       y = "%Identity",
       x = "") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = T),
         fill = "none")
```

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
# Global Statistical Summary: Mean Conservation (Bootstrap)
alignments_human2mouse_pointrange_all_global = alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_filtered %>%
  # 1. Clean labels and establish the logical factor order for the comparison
  mutate(
    status = str_replace(status, " ", "\n"),
    status = fct_relevel(
      status,
      "Human\nonly", "Mouse\nonly", "Shared", "All", 
      "Non-Immune\nBTMs", "Immune\nBTMs"
    )
  ) %>% 
  mutate(analysis = "Mean Conservation, Bootstrap") %>%
  
  # 2. Setup the visualization: Aesthetics and Faceting
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = status,
      y = identity_human2mouse,
      fill = status,
      color = status,
      group = status) +
  facet_wrap(~analysis) +
  
  # 3. Layer 1: Pointrange with bootstrapped Mean and CI
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_boot",
               geom = "pointrange",
               size = 1,
               fatten = 2,
               stroke = 0.5,
               pch = 21,
               mapping = aes(color = status),
               position = position_dodge2(0)) +
  
  # 4. Layer 2: Text labels for the precise mean values
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_boot", 
               geom = "text", 
               aes(label = after_stat(round(y, 1))), 
               hjust = -0.2, 
               size = 3,
               color = "black") +
  
  # 5. Custom scales for fill and color
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(colors$comparison,
                               "BTMs" = "#4361ee",
                               "All" = "white")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(colors$comparison,
                                "BTMs" = "#4361ee",
                                "All" = "black")) +
  
  # 6. Adjust scales and coordinate system
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +
  
  # 7. Final Theme and Legend Cleanup
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0,  hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = 10),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.1, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(0.3, 0.3, 0, 0, unit = "cm"),
        legend.position = "none",
        ggh4x.facet.nestline = element_line(colour = "black", linetype = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Status",
       y = "%Identity (Human-to-Mouse)",
       color = "",
       fill = "")
```

Plot boxplot with violin plot and unite with point-range plot

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
# Global Distribution of Conservation with Highlighted Exemplar Genes
# Violin + boxplot with highlighted exemplar genes overlaid
alignments_human2mouse_histogram_all_global = alignments_human2mouse_all_global_df_filtered %>%
  # 1. Prepare categories and factor levels
  mutate(analysis = "Distribution of conservation",
         status = str_replace(status, " ", "\n"),
         status = fct_relevel(status, "Human\nonly", "Mouse\nonly", "Shared", 
                              "All", "Non-Immune\nBTMs", "Immune\nBTMs")) %>% 
  
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = status, y = identity_human2mouse, fill = status, color = status, group = status) +
  facet_wrap(~analysis) +
  
  # 2. Main Layers: Violin for density and transparent Boxplot
  geom_violin(color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(color = status), width = 0.1, fill = NA, outliers = F) +
  
  # 3. First Color Scale: Category status
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Status", values = c(colors$comparison, "All" = "white")) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Status", 
                     values = c("Mouse\nonly" = "white", "Human\nonly" = "white", "Shared" = "white", 
                                "Immune\nBTMs" = "white", "Non-Immune\nBTMs" = "white", "All" = "black")) +
  
  # 4. Secondary Color Scale: Custom filters for highlighted genes
  new_scale_color() + 
  scale_color_manual(
     name = "Filter",
     values = c("High %Identity" = "#4361ee", "Positive correlation,\nHigh %Identity" = "#4DBBD5FF",
                "Negative correlation,\nHigh %Identity" = "#7209b7", "Low %Identity" = "red",
                "Positive correlation,\nLow %Identity" = "#CA6702", "Negative correlation,\nLow %Identity" = "#AE2012")) +
  
  # 5. Adding highlighted genes as points
  geom_point(data = alignments_human2mouse_genes_filtered %>% 
               group_by(status, filter) %>% 
               slice_head(n = 5), aes(color = filter), pch = 21, fill = "white") +
  
  # 6. Statistical annotation: Median identity labels
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "label", aes(label = after_stat(round(y, 1))),
               size = 3, hjust = -0.2, color = "black", fill = "white") +
  
  # 7. Gene Labeling: Repel prevents overlapping names
  geom_label_repel(data = alignments_human2mouse_genes_filtered %>% 
               group_by(status, filter) %>% 
               slice_head(n = 5),
                   aes(label = gene, color = filter), 
                   max.overlaps = 10000, size = 2, direction = "y", nudge_x = -0.4,
                   hjust = 0, fill = "white", box.padding = unit(0, "cm"), label.padding = unit(0.1, "cm")) +
  
  # 8. Scales, Theme, and Layout
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0.1, 0.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0.01), limits = c(50, 105)) +
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.position = "top", legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.margin = margin(0,0,0,0), legend.box.margin = margin(0,0,-10,0),
        plot.margin = margin(0.3, 0.3, 0, 0, unit = "cm")) +
  labs(x = "Status", y = "%Identity (Human-to-Mouse)", color = "", fill = "")

# Display
alignments_human2mouse_histogram_all_global

# Unite summary and distribution plots using patchwork
alignments_human2mouse_pointrange_histogram = (alignments_human2mouse_pointrange_all_global /
alignments_human2mouse_histogram_all_global) +
```

```{r fig.height=3, fig.width=10}
# Build line plot with pointrange for each gene category across timepoints

      fill = status,
```

```{r}
# Pairwise sequence alignment
library(pwalign)
#Compare two original sequences
alignment <- pairwiseAlignment(
  pattern = gene_data$peptide_human, 
  subject = gene_data$peptide_mouse, 
  substitutionMatrix = "BLOSUM62",
  type = "global", # Garante alinhamento de ponta a ponta
  gapOpening = 10,  # Penalidade padrão
  gapExtension = 0.5
)

# Get identity score
identity_global <- pid(alignment, type = "PID1")

#Convert to a df
alignment_results_pairwise <- tibble(
  hgnc_symbol       = gene_data$hgnc_symbol,
  seq_human_orig    = gene_data$peptide_human,
  seq_mouse_orig    = gene_data$peptide_mouse,
  seq_human_aligned = as.character(pattern(alignment)),
  seq_mouse_aligned = as.character(subject(alignment)),
  identity          = identity_global
) %>% 
  inner_join(genes_domain_mouse_human %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(mgi_symbol, hgnc_symbol, identity_biomart = identity, peptide_mouse, peptide_human, uniprotswissprot_human,
         filter, status, n, cor_value, p_value, r_squared, cor_label) %>% 
  distinct(),
  by = "hgnc_symbol")
```

##### Visualise structures — Prepare protein data for CD2

Fetch UniProt annotations (topology, domains, PTMs) and compute pairwise
sequence differences between human and mouse CD2 from the alignment.
These will feed into a multi-track protein annotation plot and 3D
visualisation.

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=8}
# Load tidyverse for data processing
library(tidyverse)

# Prepare sequence and annotation data for the selected gene
# Extract the row corresponding to selected_gene and keep the longest isoforms
# to ensure we have full-length sequences for comparison
gene_info <- alignment_results_pairwise %>%
  filter(hgnc_symbol == selected_gene) %>%
  mutate(
    len_mouse = nchar(seq_mouse_orig),
    len_human = nchar(seq_human_orig)
  ) %>%
  slice_max(len_human, n = 1) %>%
  slice_max(len_mouse, n = 1)

# Create a "Full Protein" annotation track covering the entire sequence
# This provides the background rectangle spanning the whole protein length
full_protein <- gene_info %>%
  select(hgnc_symbol, len_mouse, len_human, status, cor_label,
         seq_human_orig, seq_mouse_orig, filter, identity, identity_biomart,
         seq_human_aligned, seq_mouse_aligned) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("len_"), names_to = "species", values_to = "end") %>%
  group_by(hgnc_symbol, species) %>%
  slice_max(end, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    species = str_remove(species, "len_"),
    start = 1,
    interpro_short_description_human = "Full Protein",
    interpro = "Full",
    species_end = species
  ) %>%
  distinct()

# Retrieve UniProt feature annotations for CD2 (human and mouse orthologs)
# This fetches transmembrane domains, topology, and other protein features
prot_data <- drawProteins::get_features("P06729 P08920") %>%
  drawProteins::feature_to_dataframe() %>%
  mutate(description = case_when(type == "TRANSMEM" ~ "TM",
                                  type == "TOPO_DOM" & description == "Extracellular" ~ "EC",
                                  type == "TOPO_DOM" & description == "Cytoplasmic" ~ "CP",
                                  description == "NONE" ~ type,
                                  description == "" ~ type,
                                  TRUE ~ description)) %>%
  separate(entryName, sep = "_", into = c("gene", "organism"), remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(organism = str_to_title(organism))

# Identify sequence differences between human and mouse from the pairwise alignment
vec_h <- strsplit(unique(full_protein$seq_human_aligned), "")[[1]]
vec_m <- strsplit(unique(full_protein$seq_mouse_aligned), "")[[1]]

# Find positions where the aligned residues differ
diff_idx <- which(vec_h != vec_m)

# Map alignment positions back to real (ungapped) residue positions per species
mutations_base <- tibble(
  align_pos = diff_idx,
  res_h = vec_h[diff_idx],
  res_m = vec_m[diff_idx]
) %>%
  mutate(
    pos_real_human = map_int(align_pos, ~ sum(vec_h[1:.x] != "-")),
    pos_real_mouse = map_int(align_pos, ~ sum(vec_m[1:.x] != "-"))
  )

# Separate by species to track mutations in each organism's coordinate system
mutations_human <- mutations_base %>%
  filter(res_h != "-") %>%
  mutate(species = "human", x_pos = pos_real_human)

mutations_mouse <- mutations_base %>%
  filter(res_m != "-") %>%
  mutate(species = "mouse", x_pos = pos_real_mouse)

# Combine mutations into a single table formatted for ggplot annotation
mutations_plot <- bind_rows(mutations_human, mutations_mouse) %>%
  rename(organism = species) %>%
  mutate(gene = unique(gene_info$hgnc_symbol),
         organism = str_to_title(organism),
         type = "Alignment",
         description = "Mutations")

```

##### Visualize structures

draw proteins

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width= 10, paged.print=TRUE}
# Get a human-readable protein name for the y-axis label
prot_name <- unique(prot_data$entryName)

# Split UniProt features into thematic tracks for multi-panel visualisation
# Track 1: Topology — transmembrane and subcellular localisation
df_topology <- prot_data %>%
  filter(type %in% c("TOPO_DOM", "TRANSMEM", "SIGNAL")) %>%
  mutate(y_pos = 1)

# Track 2: Domains — functional regions (Ig-like, receptors, etc.)
df_features <- prot_data %>%
  filter(type %in% c("DOMAIN", "REGION", "MOTIF", "RECEPT_DOM")) %>%
  mutate(y_pos = 1.5)

# Track 3: Modifications — PTMs and natural variants
df_modifications <- prot_data %>%
  filter(type %in% c("MOD_RES", "PHOSPHO", "VARIANT")) %>%
  mutate(y_pos = 1.61)

# Alignments-derived mutation data frame
df_mutations <- mutations_plot

# Create a summary dataframe to define the background line length for each facet
# This ensures the grey backbone scales to the correct length per organism
background_lines <- prot_data %>%
  group_by(organism, gene) %>%
  summarise(max_end = max(end), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  tidyr::crossing(y_val = c(1, 1.5))

# Initialise the multi-layer protein annotation ggplot
drawprotein_uniprot_ggplot <- ggplot() +

  # Track background: grey line spanning the full protein length per facet
  geom_segment(data = background_lines,
               aes(x = 1, xend = max_end, y = y_val, yend = y_val),
               color = "grey80", size = 2) +

  # Track 1: Topology rectangles — extracellular, cytoplasmic, transmembrane
  geom_rect(data = df_topology,
            aes(xmin = begin, xmax = end,
                ymin = y_pos - 0.1, ymax = y_pos + 0.1,
                fill = description),
            color = "black", size = 0.2) +

  # Facet by organism and gene for side-by-side species comparison
  facet_wrap(~ paste(organism, gene), ncol = 1) +

  # Custom fill scale for topology track
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("EC" = "#4cc9f0",
                                "CP" = "#3a86ff",
                                "TM" = "#90A4AEFF",
                                "SIGNAL" = "#f72585"),
                    name = "Topology") +

  # Reset fill scale for the next aesthetic layer
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +

  # Track 2: Functional domains — semi-transparent rectangles with independent fill
  geom_rect(data = df_features,
            aes(xmin = begin, xmax = end,
                ymin = y_pos - 0.1, ymax = y_pos + 0.1,
                fill = description),
            color = "black", size = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako", name = "Domains") +

  # Track 3: Modification points — diamonds for phosphorylation / variants
  geom_point(data = df_modifications,
             aes(x = begin, y = y_pos + 0.02, color = type),
             size = 3, shape = 18) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("PHOSPHO" = "yellow", "VARIANT" = "red"),
                     name = "PTMs") +

  # Reset color for mutation layer
  new_scale_color() +

  # Mutation layer: violin + points to show alignment divergence density
  geom_violin(data = mutations_plot,
              aes(x = x_pos, y = 1.5, color = "Mutations"),
              fill = NA, size = 0.4, width = 0.2, scale = "count", adjust = 0.05) +
  geom_point(data = mutations_plot,
             aes(x = x_pos, y = 1.5, color = "Mutations",
                 label = paste(align_pos, res_h, res_m)),
             shape = 124, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Mutations" = "red"), name = "Alignment") +

  # Axis formatting: map y_pos to track labels
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(unique(df_topology$y_pos), unique(df_features$y_pos)),
                     labels = c("Topology", "Domains")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0.01)) +

  # Annotate domain start and end coordinates on the plot
  geom_text(aes(label = begin, y = y_pos, x = begin),
            data = df_features,
            nudge_y = 0.15, hjust = 0.5, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = end, y = y_pos, x = end),
            data = df_features,
            nudge_y = -0.15, hjust = 0.5, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = begin, y = y_pos, x = begin),
            data = df_topology,
            nudge_y = 0.15, hjust = 0.5, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = end, y = y_pos, x = end),
            data = df_topology,
            nudge_y = -0.15, hjust = 0.5, size = 3) +

  # Custom lab theme
  theme_vaxgo() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.justification = "top",
        legend.spacing.y = unit(0, "cm"),
        plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 2, 1)) +

  # Labels: include identity and correlation metrics in the title
  labs(x = "Residue position",
       y = "Features",
       title = paste0("Gene: ", unique(prot_data$gene),
                      ", UNIPROT: ", unique(prot_data$accession),
                      ". Status: ", unique(gene_info$status),
                      ". Filter: ", str_replace(unique(gene_info$filter), "\n", " "),
                      ", Correlation: ", unique(gene_info$cor_label),
                      "\nIdentity (MUSCLE, BLOSUM62): ", round(unique(gene_info$identity), 1),
                      ". Identity (BioMart): ", round(unique(gene_info$identity_biomart), 1)))

# Display the plot
drawprotein_uniprot_ggplot
```

```{r}
library(NGLVieweR)
library(dplyr)

# Define distinct colours for each domain feature to ensure clear visual separation in the 3D structure
domain_colors <- colors_all

# Prepare the domain feature table with colour assignment and residue range selection
df_features_3d <- df_features %>%
  mutate(
    color_3d = domain_colors[1:n()],
    selection = paste0(begin, "-", end)
  )

# Initialise NGLVieweR with CD2 human AlphaFold structure
# Set orthographic camera, high sample level for antialiasing, and a transparent ribbon backbone
view_domain <- NGLVieweR(here::here("Structures", "CD2_HumanAF-P06729-F1-model_v6.pdb")) %>%
  stageParameters(
    backgroundColor = "white",
    cameraType = "orthographic",
    clipDist = 0,
    sampleLevel = 4,
    preserveDrawingBuffer = TRUE
  ) %>%
  addRepresentation("cartoon", param = list(color = "#D3D3D3", opacity = 0.2))

# Overlay each domain with its assigned colour as a cartoon representation
for (i in seq_len(nrow(df_features_3d))) {
  current_color <- as.character(df_features_3d$color_3d[i])
  current_sele  <- as.character(df_features_3d$selection[i])
  if (!is.na(current_color)) {
    view_domain <- view_domain %>%
      addRepresentation("cartoon", param = list(
        sele = current_sele,
        color = current_color,
        opacity = 1
      ))
  }
}

# Render and rotate for optimal viewing angle
view_domain
view_domain <- view_domain %>%
  NGLVieweR::setRotation(c(0, 1.57, 0)) %>%
  NGLVieweR::setSelection("*")
view_domain

# Annotate chains in the PDB object: assign a single-letter code per domain for downstream visualisation
for (i in seq_len(nrow(df_features_3d))) {
  desc_char <- toupper(substr(as.character(df_features_3d$description[i]), 1, 1))
  res_range <- as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(as.character(df_features_3d$selection[i]), "-")))
  sele <- atom.select(pdb, resno = res_range[1]:res_range[2])
  if (length(sele$atom) > 0) {
    pdb$atom$chain[sele$atom] <- desc_char
  }
}

# Save the chain-annotated PDB for later use
write.pdb(pdb, file = here("Structures", "cd2_com_chains.pdb"))
```
